items.question: How does Arda relate to existing databases?
items.answer: Arda manages access, cataloging, governance and services around existing sources. Whether data needs to be synchronized or transformed depends on the use case and integration plan. Building a catalog does not require replacing every business system first.

items.question: How do Arda and Karda divide their roles?
items.answer: They are peer platforms. Arda manages data assets, standards, quality and lineage for controlled data supply. Karda manages documents and professional experience for knowledge retrieval and citation. Agent applications can use either service or combine them according to the task.

items.question: Does Arda handle knowledge Q&A or agent orchestration?
items.answer: Arda focuses on data assets, governance and supply as a foundation for analytics and intelligent applications. Knowledge Q&A, model inference and agent orchestration belong to the corresponding products, which can be combined for your use case.

items.question: How can I try Arda?
items.answer: Arda currently uses invitation-only subscriptions. Contact us with your data sources, priority use case and security requirements to define a trial. Features, supported sources and delivery arrangements depend on the agreed access plan.

items.question: How is Karda different from a file store or document library?
items.answer: File stores focus on saving and collaborating on files. Karda primarily prepares and supplies retrievable, citable knowledge to agent applications. People maintain and verify content, with search as a supporting activity. Original materials remain the basis for verification; existing document systems need not all be replaced.

items.question: How does Karda relate to Arda?
items.answer: Arda and Karda are peer platform products. Arda manages data, standards, quality and lineage for controlled data supply. Karda manages documents and professional experience for knowledge retrieval and citation. Both support agent applications and can be used separately or together, without a hierarchy between them.

items.question: Can every agent use an added knowledge library?
items.answer: Adding content does not make it public. Each application needs a defined knowledge scope, and retrieval and citation must respect that authorization. Stewards and people using search also follow their own access boundaries.

items.question: Does Karda perform the agent’s business tasks?
items.answer: Karda provides knowledge processing, organization, retrieval and source evidence. The agent application generates answers, combines tools and carries out business tasks. Results still depend on content quality, retrieval and application design; important decisions require checking sources and applicability.

items.question: How do we get started?
items.answer: Tell us which business tasks the agent application handles, the knowledge sources it needs and its access scope. Start with one clear scenario and agree on intake, stewardship and authorization.
